{{Quote|Poisons? Toxins? Destroy them from space with bombs!''"<br />"''As I have explained before, Darth Azard, we're not here to make the inhabitants really, really sick. We're here to make certain they all ''die''.|Darth Azard and Vul Isen|<ref name="Legacy 49" />}}
'''Viral spores''' were deadly biological weapons developed by the [[One Sith]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Vul Isen]] during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]] as a means of pacifying rebellious worlds without committing substantial Imperial forces. They were capable of poisoning all living organisms on a planet's oceans within days, effectively rendering it uninhabitable. These viral spores were deployed in canisters and were used to great effect as part of the [[Final Protocol]] as part of the [[Genocide on Dac|Genocide of Mon Calamari]] on [[Dac/Legends|Dac]]. Later, [[Sith–Imperial attack ship]]s of [[Quad Victor|Squadron Quad Victor]] deployed these during the [[Devastation of Da Soocha|destruction]] of [[Da Soocha]].

==Description==
{{Quote|We no longer need Death Stars or Galaxy Guns to destroy planets. Merely the contents of this vial poured into the planet's water system.|Vul Isen, while on Utapau|<ref name="Legacy 50" />}}
[[File:Imsoproud.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Vul Isen examines his viral spores on Utapau.]]
Viral spores were a biological weapon<ref name="Legacy 47" /> created by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Vul Isen]] in [[137 ABY]], during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]].<ref name="Legacy 32" /> Isen developed multiple strains of the viral-type toxin between 137 and [[138 ABY]], and each was capable of [[Poison/Legends|poisoning]] an entire [[Planet/Legends|planet]].<ref name="Legacy 47" /><ref name="Legacy 50" /><ref name="Legacy 48" /> Once released into a world's [[Water/Legends|waters]], viral spores were<ref name="Legacy 47" /> immediately<ref name="Legacy 50" /> carried and spread by currents, [[Death/Legends|killing]] every living thing that they encountered. Within one [[Standard week/Legends|week]], the entirety of a world, even one nearly completely covered in [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]], was affected, and nothing remained alive.<ref name="Legacy 47" />

Isen's initial viral spore formulas required multiple canisters full of the toxins to be inserted into a planet's waters.<ref name="Legacy 48" /> However, his final strain, which took the form of a light [[Color/Legends|green]] liquid, was potent enough that a single vial&mdash;small enough to fit inside the [[Limb/Legends|hand]] of a [[Human/Legends|Human]] or a [[Givin/Legends|Givin]]&mdash;contained sufficient destructive power for an entire world.<ref name="Legacy 50" /> Isen created the toxins as a means of [[Speciecide|punishing]] planetary populations who earned the wrath of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]], an organization which the scientist served.<ref name="Legacy 47" /> He believed that the mere threat of their use would be able to pacify rebellion against the Empire.<ref name="Legacy 49">[[Legacy (2006) 49|''Legacy'' (2006) 49]]</ref>

The different formulas were developed for use against various [[Species/Legends|species]], whose differing biological systems reacted uniquely to the toxins' effects. Isen's original formula [[Final Protocol|targeted]] the population of the planet [[Dac/Legends|Dac]],<ref name="Legacy 47" /> a world which teemed with a vast variety of life,<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and his final strain was developed for use on the planet [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]]. During the latter formula's development, scientific experiments performed on test subjects from the native [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'an]] and [[Utai/Legends|Utai]] species helped Isen create a formula that would target both species.<ref name="Legacy 49" /> Although he was able to render himself immune to its effects,<ref name="Legacy 50" /> the scientist speculated that the third strain, which was adaptable, could affect any species in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Legacy 49" />

==History==
{{Quote|I've had the viral spores placed for months. Once I release them, the currents will carry the spore throughout the planet. Within a week, everything on Dac will be dead, and we can both go on to productive work elsewhere.|Vul Isen, speaking to Darth Azard on Dac|<ref name="Legacy 47" />}}
Vul Isen developed viral spores in 137 ABY while creating experimental viruses for use on the population of the planet Dac. [[Darth Krayt]], [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] and [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], ordered a [[Genocide on Dac|genocide]] of the world's native [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] in that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], and Imperial forces were sent to Dac to oversee their extermination. Isen and [[Darth Azard]], both members of Krayt's [[One Sith]], were dispatched planetside to lead the operation. Although Krayt's orders specified that only the Mon Calamari were to die, Isen created viral spores in the hope of poisoning the entire planet and wiping out every native species.<ref name="Legacy 32" /> To his end, he placed the spores in strategic locations throughout the planet and waited for the order to release them.<ref name="Legacy 47" /> After Krayt's servant [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Darth Wyyrlok]] attempted to kill his [[Sith Master/Legends|Master]] and usurped the throne,<ref name="Legacy 31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref> the new [[Regent/Legends|Regent]] of the Empire instructed Isen to release viral spores. Isen did so, and within three days, millions of Dac's natives had succumbed to its effects. The sheer number of corpses that floated to the oceans' surfaces caused members of the [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Squadron/Legends|unit]] [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] to falsely observe from [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] that a new landmass had formed. When they realized that what they saw were bodies, they contacted their superiors within the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]]. Alliance [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gar Stazi]] organized a massive [[evacuation of Dac]], and was able to ferry nearly twenty percent of the planet's various [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species offworld before the effects of the viral spores encompassed the entire planet.<ref name="Legacy 47" />

The use of viral spores to poison Dac enraged many citizens of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]],<ref name="Legacy War 2">[[Legacy — War 2|''Legacy — War'' 2]]</ref> among them the former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Cade Skywalker]].<ref name="Legacy 48" /> Skywalker had recently declared a personal war against the Sith,<ref name="Legacy 46">[[Legacy (2006) 46|''Legacy'' (2006) 46]]</ref> and Isen, whom the former Jedi declared the "[[Vul Isen|Butcher of Dac]]," became his first target. Skywalker surmised that killing Isen and neutralizing his ability to create biological weapons would deal the Sith a considerable blow. While Skywalker [[Hunting/Legends|hunted]] for his foe, Isen and Azard arrived at the planet [[Da Soocha]] aboard the Sith&ndash;Imperial [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] ''[[War Hammer]]''. The Empire had learned that [[Azzim Anjiliac Atirue]], a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] based out of Da Soocha's [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Napdu]], had recently given refuge to Mon Calamari refugees, and as such, Azard ordered viral spores to be inserted into Da Soocha's oceans while Azzim's [[Maya Armus|spa]] on Napdu was [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombarded]] by the ''War Hammer''{{'s}} turbolasers. Insertion of canisters full of the toxin was performed by the Imperial [[Bomber/Legends|bomber]] squadron [[Quad Victor]].<ref name="Legacy 48" />
